title: Gotham VS Song
transcript: Gotham Chess, the biggest chess creator ever, is facing in a match Julien Song, the biggest French chess creator. And I wanted to show you this position from one of their games because this is exactly the type of stuff that I love. In this position, Julien has a knight for two extra pawns that white has, but things are not very straightforward. The black king is quite open and the black pawns are completely scattered around the board. In this position, Levy attacks the bishop on C5 with his knight. Now, this creates a bunch of problems for the black position because first of all, the knight here in the center is simply hanging at the moment. If Julien tries to move the knight away to save it from the attack, well, now white can gain the initiative with F4 attacking the center. And after queen to E2, white is all of a sudden creating a lot of chances, which is why in this position Julien decided to go all in and he played queen to C7, sacrificing the knight in the center because if the knight is taken, this would simply result in a checkmate. Which is exactly why Gotham Chess now takes a step away from this line. But guys, look at all of the activity of these pieces and how the queen and rook are all pointing at this white king. We must look for sacrifices and that is exactly what Julien did and he decided to sacrifice his war steed with knight to C2, another brilliant sacrifice. International Master Levy Rozman decides to take the steed. And now, the king hunt begins. Bishop takes A3 check. We open up the battery of the queen and rook. The king goes back to safety. Queen to C2 check pushes the king to the side, but the bishop is of course defended, but Julien is an international master for a reason. He now trades the bishops and plays the very accurate A4, which cannot be ignored. But of course, this also kind of looks like a free pawn, but black is simply trying to open up the lines here. And now, rook to C4 continues the attack now threatening to take with a checkmate on A4. The king can simply go to A1 and now there's not going to be a pin on the knight. If you now take the pawn, the knight is simply going to be able to take the rook and now white is out of danger. Right? Not exactly. In this position, Julien decided to serve Gotham Chess his own medicine and HE SACRIFICED THE ROOK! Rook takes A4 anyway because after the knight captures, the queen can take back with a check and look at how exposed this king is. And now, queen to B4 puts the last nail in this coffin because if the king moves to the A file, now the rook is going to come with a checkmate in two moves. And if the king moves to the C file, the rook is going to come to C8 and look at the harmony between the queen and the knight preventing the escape of the white king to the king side, meaning that this would actually be just another checkmate in two moves. Whoever said that creators cannot play incredible chess, huh?
